text:
Oshodi. 6pm. The bus stop is full. The conductor is shouting. But the door is jammed.

That's most businesses selling online in Nigeria right now. The ads bring people to the bus stop. The leaks stop them getting in.

Swipe to find the leak jamming your door. Then comment your number, 1 to 5, and I'll reply with the first fix.

#lagosbusiness #smallbusinessnigeria #instagramvendor #salesfunnel #lagoslogic
alts: Slide 1 of 10. For anyone selling online in Nigeria Your ads are not the problem. Your danfo door is jammed. Illustration: a yellow Lagos danfo bus with its door taped shut, a conductor shouting and a crowd waiting at the bus stop.

Slide 2 of 10. Picture this Oshodi. 6pm. Everybody wants to go home. So what does the conductor do? The conductor is shouting "Oshodi! Oshodi!" The bus stop is full. People are ready. But the door is jammed.
Slide 3 of 10. That's what boosting a post is. He shouts louder. Paying more money to shout at people who still can't get in. More boost. More "How much?" Same zero transfers.

Slide 4 of 10. Before you buy more fuel Ad money is fuel. Fuel is expensive. Swipe. Count your leaks. Every business online is a danfo. Before you spend one more naira on ads, check the 5 places your passengers fall off.

Slide 5 of 10. The conductor shouts "Enter! Enter!" but never says where the bus is going. Your post says "Quality products at affordable prices." Nobody can tell if this bus is for them. Shout the destination: who it is for, what they get.
Slide 6 of 10. The bus looks like one chance. No real photos. No reviews. No delivery proof. Nobody enters a bus they don't trust. Show proof before you ask for money.
Slide 7 of 10. The door is jammed. "DM for price." "Check your DM." Replies six hours later. They wanted to enter. You made it hard. Every extra step = one passenger walking to the next bus.
Slide 8 of 10. The passenger said "Wait, make I buy gala." The bus zoomed off. "Let me check my account." "I'll pay Friday." Then you never messaged again. "I'll get back to you" is not a no.

Slide 9 of 10. The driver doesn't know which route pays. You boosted five posts. You can't say which one brought the sale. So you keep paying for the empty route. Ask every buyer: where did you see us?

text:
Most business owners I talk to think their ads are the problem.

Usually the ads are working. People arrive. Then they hit one of five leaks: the message, trust, friction, follow up or measurement.

I explained it with the most Lagos thing I know: a danfo with a jammed door.

Which leak costs your business the most?

I read two Nairaland threads on “DM for price”. Hundreds of replies. Buyers did not hold back.

Slide 3 is the one that stings.

My take: showing your price doesn't scare serious buyers. It filters out the ones who were never going to pay. Then give people a better reason to DM: size, colour, delivery date, a quote for their space.

Comment LEAK and I'll send you the 5 minute leak check I run on every page before it goes live.

#dmforprice #instagramvendor #lagosvendors #naijabusiness #onlinebusinessnigeria
alts: Slide 1 of 8. Straight from Nairaland What buyers say about "DM for price" behind your back Illustration: a phone inbox full of unread messages saying How much, Price pls, How much last and hm.

Slide 2 of 8. The question Somebody asked Nairaland why vendors do this. The thread pulled 42,692 views. Quote from pocohantas, Nairaland · Sept 2020: They will post a very fine item, then write "DM for price". When you comment to ask them for the price, they will reply "Check your DM". Why do they do this? What are they hiding?

Slide 3 of 8. Slide 3. I warned you. Con artist. For hiding a price. Quote from excellence44, Nairaland · Sept 2020: Whenever I see dm or WhatsApp for price I just jump and pass. They are simply unserious con artist.

Slide 4 of 8. Why they think it Hidden price reads as: "They will price me by my profile picture." Quote from Wickedtruths, Nairaland · Sept 2020: What they do is that they check your profile pics and online profile before giving you a price ... most serious buyers who are really interested don't bother sending DMs. They move on to the next seller with available pricing and negotiate.

Slide 5 of 8. Where the buyer goes instead Your "DM for price" is a free advert for Jumia. Quote from Ayemileto, Nairaland · Sept 2020: There are times I have interest in purchasing a product but won't DM ... to ask for price. Instead, I will simply go on Jumia and checkout their prices.

Slide 6 of 8. Fair is fair Some products do need a conversation. Zobo. With "DM for price". Quote from Tayeni, Nairaland · Sept 2020: Your normal Instagram ad won't tell a prospect all the benefits ... that will justify high prices in some expensive items ... Everyday items are an exception to this rule. ... They too parrot check your DM on their a zobo drinks adverts.

Slide 7 of 8. The fix Show the price. Then give a better reason to DM. Example prices. Use yours. Before: New arrivals! DM for price. After · everyday item: ₦18,500. Lagos delivery in 24 hours. DM "SIZE" and I'll confirm your fit. After · big ticket: From ₦350,000. Built to fit your space. DM "QUOTE" with your room size.
